episode.title: Recover long streamed answers after mid-stream transport cuts without replaying or duplicating delivered text

evidence_units.claim: Issue #7832 reports that large headless/YOLO generations fail when a gateway closes the streaming socket after several minutes. The reported root cause is that transport retry is gated on `!streamYieldedChunk`; thinking/reasoning chunks arrive early, so a later socket close is not retried even though the answer is incomplete.
The pinned implementation ref is commit d7c0d4ca7706ede8d1c8877a20343aa3e1d40bf5, whose parent is 3d1eba935f6a75d9e67adf667002700c5c592ec2. The commit lists two changed files and a +1,229/-109 diff.

The implementation widens the replay gate from any yielded chunk to visible output, then adds continuation recovery for cuts that already delivered answer text. It keeps delivered text, asks the model to resume, and emits `{ RETRY, isContinuation: true }` so the caller keeps its existing text buffer.

Recovery scaffolding is constructed only in the request and is not written to history. On success, the delivered prefix is merged into the trailing model turn, replayed overlap is deduplicated, continuation is bounded to three attempts, and cuts that delivered a function call are excluded because inserting a user turn before its function response would produce an invalid provider sequence.

The pinned change extracts `resetTransportContinuation()` and calls it before the transport replay and reactive compression branches emit a plain non-continuation RETRY. This prevents the suppress-next-retry arm from leaving stale continuation text that the UI discarded but a later success would merge into history.

The continuation buffer no longer uses raw accumulation across attempts. A per-attempt buffer is folded into the accumulated buffer in the catch path through `getRecoveryContinuationSuffix`, removing overlap at the attempt boundary so an intermediate replay cannot be baked into later requests or durable history.

The replay gate is made an exact complement of the continuation gate: replay is allowed only when the accumulated continuation buffer is empty, while a retryable cut after any previously delivered text continues even if the current attempt yielded only a thought part or nothing. The old test asserting that a later no-output cut drops continuation is rewritten to assert that the text survives into the next request and history.

The retry event has distinct caller-visible semantics: plain RETRY discards the current streamed output, while the continuation marker preserves the text already shown. The commit explicitly aligns the continuation shape with the existing MAX_TOKENS recovery path and notes that rate-limit and invalid-stream branches already re-send after streamed thought content.

`packages/core/src/core/geminiChat.test.ts` adds branch-specific reset tests, updates the later-cut/no-current-output behavior, and covers delivered-text merge positions involving thought parts. The commit reports the final suite at 277 passing tests in `geminiChat.test.ts`.
The pinned commit reports that the new regression tests fail when the source change is removed and that `tsc --noEmit` and eslint are clean.
